## ✅ Executive Summary
This readout covers 2 functional requirements for Bulk Invoice Export for Enterprise Accounts, assessed at Medium overall impact. Dependency sequencing could not be assessed — dependency-graph.mmd has not yet been generated for this program. The biggest risk is that a 50,000-invoice export running against the live Billing Service database could contend with normal billing write traffic during peak hours. One open question remains, on whether exports should run against a read replica instead of the primary database. A data-quality flag is also carried forward: the Billing Service CMDB entry is over a year old, so the touch analysis below should be treated as provisional.

## Requirements

### FR-001: Scheduled Bulk Invoice Export
**Statement:** As an enterprise account admin, I want to schedule a recurring bulk export of my organization's invoices, so that I can feed them into our internal finance systems without manual downloads.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
| Category | Boundary Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Performance | Export of up to 50,000 invoices must complete within 10 minutes | Stakeholder interview, Enterprise Ops |

### FR-002: Export Access Restricted by Role
**Statement:** As a system, I must restrict bulk export access to users holding the Billing Admin role, so that invoice data isn't exposed to unauthorized staff.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
| Category | Boundary Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Security | Only users with the Billing Admin role may trigger or download an export | Security team standard |

## Assumptions, Constraints, Risks & Open Questions

### Assumptions
- **Existing role model covers Billing Admin** (underlies FR-002): We assume the Billing Admin role already exists in the identity system and does not need to be created.

### Constraints
- **No new data warehouse** (constrains FR-001): Exports must be generated from the existing Billing Service database; no new data warehouse or ETL pipeline may be introduced.

### Risks
- **Large exports could contend with billing writes** (affects FR-001, program-level): A 50,000-invoice export running against the live Billing Service database could contend with normal billing write traffic during peak hours.

### Open Questions
- FR-001 (Performance): TBD whether exports should run against a read replica instead of the primary Billing Service database to avoid write contention.

## External Dependencies
- Export files are delivered via the existing SFTP gateway; no new external vendor required.

## Flags & Data Quality
- CMDB entry for Billing Service was last verified 412 days ago; treat the touch analysis above as provisional pending a refreshed CMDB sync.
